stories.headline: Denver council committee advances permanent aid program for businesses hurt by city construction
stories.summary:
A Denver City Council committee on Tuesday advanced two ordinances that would write the city's program for small businesses hurt by construction into law and require money to be set aside for it. The Finance and Business Committee approved one ordinance creating the Business Impact Opportunity Program, known as the BIO Fund, and another creating a special revenue fund for it. Both now go to the full council. A sponsor said the goal is for the program to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

Councilmembers Amanda Sawyer, Chris Hinds and Flor Alvidrez sponsored the measures. Hinds, who chairs the committee, said the program has operated entirely within the city's executive branch. He said the city's economist and Department of Finance found that sales tax collections in the Colfax, Bluebird and Mayfair business improvement districts along East Colfax were lower once bus rapid transit construction began than in the same months a year earlier. He did not give figures.

Under the proposal, city-funded projects costing $10 million to $25 million and lasting more than 12 months would set aside at least 1% of their budgeted cost. Projects of $25 million or more lasting more than 18 months would set aside between 1% and 5%. Projects under $10 million would not be covered. Sponsors said the money must come from the general fund because the city has not found a dedicated source.

Businesses with annual gross revenue of $100,000 or less could receive grants of up to 10% of that revenue, while larger businesses could receive at least $15,000. Hinds said the city will not fund Aurora businesses along the bus rapid transit line. City administrative costs would be capped at 7%, and unspent money would roll over from year to year.

stories.headline: Jokic, Murray lead Nuggets past Pelicans 116-108 for New Orleans' sixth straight loss
stories.summary:
Nikola Jokic had 26 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists, and the Denver Nuggets outlasted the New Orleans Pelicans 116-108 on Saturday night in New Orleans. The result extended the Pelicans' losing streak to six games.

Jamal Murray added 23 points, seven rebounds and nine assists for Denver. The Nuggets' two stars combined for 49 points and 19 assists in the road win.

Denver guard DeMar DeRozan was among the players in the rotation against New Orleans, which started guard Jaron Pierre Jr. The Nuggets entered the weekend with a 6-4 record, and the victory continued a stretch in which the team has leaned heavily on Jokic and Murray.

stories.headline: Broncos reach bye week at 7-2 after win over Chiefs lifts them into first in AFC West
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos have reached their bye week nine games into the season with a 7-2 record, putting them in strong position given a difficult early schedule. Their record projects to at least nine more games, eight in the regular season and at least one in the playoffs.

A Week 8 win over the Kansas City Chiefs pushed Denver into first place in the AFC West. That game required a number of key plays in the biggest moments, and 9News columnist Mike Klis singled out two of them in a ranking of the team's top nine plays through the first nine games.

With the bye week giving players a chance to recover, the Broncos will resume play with a lead in the division. Denver will continue to face the remainder of its divisional schedule as it pursues a playoff spot.

stories.headline: Blackwood, Lehkonen lead Avalanche past Canadiens 4-1 in Montreal
stories.summary:
Goaltender Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves and Artturi Lehkonen had a two-point night as the Colorado Avalanche defeated the Montreal Canadiens 4-1 at Centre Bell on Saturday.

Fedor Svechkov, Brock Nelson and Nicolas Roy each added goals for Colorado. Veteran defenseman Brent Burns played in his 1,600th regular-season NHL game, and defenseman Alex Gagne made his NHL debut.

The win came after the Avalanche lost in overtime at Ottawa on Nov. 13, a game in which the team lost forwards Nathan MacKinnon and defenseman Cale Makar to lower-body injuries.

stories.headline: Boulder police identify all people sought in Halloween party shooting that killed CU student
stories.summary:
Boulder police say everyone seen in security photos and video released after a Halloween party shooting has now been identified. Police spokesperson Dionne Waugh confirmed the update Thursday. Prosecutors are considering additional charges, and police said any further arrests or charges would be announced by news release.

The primary suspect, Omar Perez, 18, faces murder and related charges in the death of Luca Hanlon, 19, a University of Colorado Boulder student. The shooting happened at an off-campus party in the University Hill neighborhood on Oct. 31. Prosecutors successfully argued in court Tuesday to have Perez held without bond, and his preliminary hearing is set for Feb. 10, 2027.

According to an arrest affidavit, officers first went to a home off Marine Street around 9:58 p.m. on a noise complaint and issued a nuisance-party citation, after which hundreds of people left. Officers returned at 11:28 p.m. after a report of gunshots. Witnesses said Perez returned with six others, was asked to leave, and a scuffle followed. A witness said Perez appeared to be wearing a SWAT uniform and a "Purge" mask.

The affidavit says a resident put Perez in a headlock, and Perez allegedly pulled a gun and fired, shooting Hanlon in the neck and another 19-year-old student in the leg. Hanlon died the next day at Boulder Community Health. The affidavit also says Perez's sister saw the photos police released, which helped lead to his arrest.

stories.headline: Cherry Creek gets another sushi restaurant as Denver-area openings and closings continue
stories.summary:
Among the notable restaurant openings this week is Sushi 37, a new Cherry Creek sushi spot at 2817 E. 3rd Ave. in the former Derecho space. It is the second sushi restaurant from SYC Concepts, following Sushi by SYC earlier this year. The restaurant is offering 20% off the entire meal through Nov. 25.

Several Mexican restaurants also expanded. Savina's Mexican Kitchen, the Brinkerhoff Hospitality Group spinoff of the La Loma restaurants, opened a Loveland location, its first new site since a 2025 name change. Carrera's Tacos of Centennial added a to-go location inside the Federal Kitchens commissary on Federal Boulevard in Denver, and El Pollo Loco opened a fifth metro-area location in Aurora.

On the closing side, Centro Mexican Kitchen in Boulder shut down after 20 years on Pearl Street. The Big Red F restaurant group plans to reopen the space as a "mountain Mexican" concept called Altura, possibly as early as next month. Arvada's LUKI Brewing also closed after six years; its owners had cited a 30% drop in sales among other challenges when announcing the closure in April.

Other openings listed include Corner on Madison, Doubles Club, PopUP Bagels in Boulder and Side Quest Wings.

stories.headline: Hyperscale data centers arrive in Colorado as regulation lags behind public opposition
stories.summary:
A new era of hyperscale data centers built for artificial intelligence has begun in Colorado, and governments and regulators are struggling to keep pace. The facilities are drawing strong public reaction across the state.

The Denver Post reports that Coloradans have responded with fist fights, shouts of "shame," litigation, petitions and public comment sessions that stretch past midnight. Pushback has been described as near universal.

Despite the opposition, the large-scale projects are moving forward while rules governing them remain behind the pace of development. The article examines how state and local governments are handling the arrival of the facilities.

stories.headline: Fog Saturday gives way to sunshine in Denver, with mild weather through Tuesday
stories.summary:
Denver's Saturday began with fog and mist and temperatures near 37 degrees. Fog was expected to linger into late morning before temperatures climb toward a high near 53, with a 20% chance of rain showers in the afternoon. The National Weather Service had no watches, warnings or advisories posted, but drivers were urged to use headlights and leave extra room where visibility drops.

Saturday night brings another slight chance of showers before fog redevelops, with lows around 34. Sunday may start foggy, but skies should turn sunny after 10 a.m. with a high near 59. Monday and Tuesday are forecast to be sunny or mostly sunny, with highs near 63 and 62.

Wednesday and Thursday remain mostly sunny but cooler, with highs near 58 and 55. Rain and snow showers become likely Friday, with a 55% chance of precipitation and a high near 53. In the mountains, light snow showers were possible Saturday afternoon and evening, especially at the highest elevations.

weather.notable: Nearly 7 degrees above the average high for this time of year.

topStory.headline: Lutnick Faces Scrutiny Over Resistance to Tighter Nvidia Chip Controls as Family Firm's Ties to Industry Draw Attention
topStory.summary:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been advocating a less stringent version of proposed federal controls on sales of advanced Nvidia chips to data centers in Southeast Asia, according to a report summarized from The New York Times. Some of those data centers are clients of Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm Lutnick led before joining the Trump administration. One example is a data center known as A201 in southern Malaysia, which is due to open next year with hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia servers and plans to supply computing power to a Chinese technology company. The arrangement is legal, but it sidesteps U.S. rules barring sales of the most advanced AI chips directly to Chinese firms.

The issue has exposed divisions inside the administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Treasury, Defense and State departments and the U.S. Trade Representative's office had supported placing Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company suspected of helping channel Nvidia chips to China, on a restricted entity list for months. He pointed to the Commerce Department as the agency responsible for acting. Axios reported that Lutnick repeatedly resisted efforts to crack down on Megaspeed despite President Trump authorizing fresh export restrictions, and that he faced pressure from White House and intelligence officials. Axios also reported that Lutnick received a highly classified intelligence warning about alleged links between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy.

Cantor Fitzgerald is now run by Lutnick's sons, Brandon and Kyle, after Lutnick transferred his ownership stake to his children through trusts when he joined the administration in February 2025. The firm has reported investments in Nvidia and helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies tied to the chipmaker's AI business. In September it hosted Huang and other senior Nvidia executives at investor meetings in New York. A CNBC analysis of securities filings found Cantor's reported Nvidia holdings fell by nearly 50% between September 2025 and March 2026, from more than 3.5 million shares at the end of 2024 to 1.78 million. Cantor has not publicly explained the reduction but has said the positions in its filings largely reflected client swap transactions rather than substantial standalone investments.

The dispute reflects a roughly two-year internal debate over how far to restrict chip sales to data centers outside China that serve Chinese customers. China hawks view the facilities as a way for Beijing to circumvent the export ban, while Lutnick and others argue against limiting U.S. companies' ability to sell in Asia. The more stringent proposals under consideration would give the U.S. government greater oversight of chip sales to international data centers and could reduce Nvidia's business. Lutnick's approach has drawn criticism from lawmakers and other administration officials. No evidence has been reported that the family's business interests influenced his government decisions or that his sons received confidential intelligence.

The outcome will determine how tightly the United States polices indirect access to advanced AI computing by Chinese firms, and whether the Commerce Department acts on the Megaspeed designation. Questions about potential conflicts of interest are likely to draw continued attention from lawmakers as the rules are finalized.
